title: What changes will LLM AI-powered NPCs bring to the gaming world? I'm implementing LLM AI Players in my game and you will be able to interact with them as real players, I tested and had lots of fun with it while playing but I wonder if the gamer community would. Do gamers want AI in games?
author: AetherianChronicles

comments.author: rickikicks
comments.body:
I work with AI developer job (not game dev). I have been moderately impressed with it as a tool for assistance, and thoroughly disappointed in it as a technical savant when trying to incorporate it into a precise tool to automate tasks.

It can be very creative when you ask it to be, but here's what I'm interested in finding out about it when it comes to using it to power the npcs in games:

1. Can it be varying enough between different characters to give them different personalities, and stay consistent with the personality it gives each individual npc?

2. Will it always be evolving and fresh or are there always going to be noticeable quirks or terms it uses to the point it makes things worse? 

What I mean by that is, If you live in the world of GTA long enough, you're going to know how each type of npc is going to react. All the way down to their repeating dialog. This one can't be answered right away and will talk time and real world implementation, but humans eventually pick up mannerisms subliminally. They will be able to discern if AI is being used to make the npc move and talk if AI fails to pass this check. Then, what would make it worse is that every game sharing the same LLM to run their npcs will have the same repetitive traits across multiple games making them all just blend together.

comments.author: kokutouchichi
comments.body:
I've dabbled with this some and I found it really cool and compelling but the main thing that's holding this back from being more widely adopted is the cost. Many of the ai run NPC platforms that currently exist that allow you to do this have fees and quotas on the number of interactions you can have as well as limits to the number of interactions. That's an additional and significant cost the developer has to take on.

Until this can run locally on the players machine at no additional cost I don't see it as a viable solution yet. But the pace is on track to achieve this soon so who knows

replies.author: AetherianChronicles
replies.body: Yes, the cost can be very challenging but there are a few ways of spinning this around and hopefully, in the future, it will be more accessible. I am implementing this AI in my game, me and my team don't have much funding but we are working hard to display this feature in our game releasing in March. If you are interested any help is [really appreciated](https://aetherianchronicles.com/)

comments.author: Southern_Sun_2106
comments.body:
check out Mantella and AI Follower Framework mods for Skyrim. There is also a naughty VR mod that plugs into AI Follower Framework. The mods give a degree of agency to NPCs where they can attack you, forgive you, follow you, have memories of adventures, and talk to other AI NPCs.   
  
The mods are super-fun! I mean, the sky is the limit, Skyrim comes to life with endless stories. If anyone wants a glimpse of the future of gaming, this is available now.  
  
There is a strong following, including many people contributing and helping, adding features. Now, why are they not 'mainstream'? Install can be challenging, and that's the main issue. But the communities on discord are very helpful, and help solve most if not all issues.

Of course, there was lots of AI scaremongering happening recently. Hopefully, it will go away. But I bet if install is solved (the vast majority, I suspect, still don't know what OpenRouter is, nor how to copy/paste API); and a simple AI toggle is added, many will try it, and will be hooked. It is hard to impossible to return to 'no-AI' games once you experience the magic of AI.

I also hope AI will breath in new life into the many cool old titles that are out there.
